lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Afterparty at the Heat Death, one seventeen point four. The top of the dial, and the end of everything. Come in. It's warm.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: This is DJ Entropy, at the last party in the universe. Plenty of room on the floor, love. There always is, now.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Afterparty at the Heat Death. Three guys, a nebula, and you. That's a crowd, love. That's a proper crowd.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Afterparty at the Heat Death. The stars are going out. We've still got the light over the decks. Come and stand near it.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Good morning from the end of the universe. There isn't a morning any more, technically. We do one anyway.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Afterparty at the Heat Death. The beat's slowing down. That's all right. So is everything. We'll go together.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Let me introduce tonight's crowd. On the left, Dov. In the middle, Wendell. On the right, a third guy, who has never told us his name. At this point, love, it would be rude to ask.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: And behind them, about forty light years wide, swaying, that's Lorraine. Lorraine's a nebula. She has never missed a night.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: If you've noticed the music getting slower, you're right. We lose a few beats a minute every hour. Everything does, out here.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: It's not the end of the song, love. It's the song getting comfortable. It's taking its shoes off.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: There's one light left above the decks. A little warm bulb. It's the brightest thing for a very long way, in every direction.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: So if you're lost out there, look for it. That's us. Come in. Mind the cables.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Lorraine's glowing a bit pinker tonight. That's how you know she's enjoying it. Nebulas haven't got hands, so she can't put them in the air.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: She does the next best thing. She's making a star, very slowly, just for the drop. It'll be ready in about a million years. We'll wait.

lines.speaker: Dov
lines.text: Can you play the one from the beginning?

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Dov wants the one from the beginning. Love, they're all from the beginning. Everything is.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: But I know the one you mean. Here it is. A little slower than it used to be. Aren't we all.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: This set is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders, the last company still trading. Years ago they sent a ladder out here, with a note on it. It said, up is a choice.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: We leaned it against the dark. Nobody's had the heart to climb it. It's just nice to know it's there.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: There's a ship out there. A relay ship, lights on, drifting up the dial. Hello, love. You came all this way. Not many do, any more.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: There's room by the speakers. The guys will budge up.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Bev. Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Bev. You found us. All the way out here.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I'm still looking for my song.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: I know, love. Stay on the line. If it's anywhere, it's here. Everything ends up here, in the end.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: A little science, for anyone wondering. The heat death means everything ends up the same temperature. Nothing warmer than anything else.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Which is why we dance. Every step, we're a little bit warmer than the dark. That's the whole idea, love. That's the rave.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The third guy just did a spin. Nobody has ever seen him spin. Wendell had to sit down. Lorraine went bright blue.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: I don't know what it means, love. I've written it down.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Excuse me, everybody. Quick dedication. Look up, just there, to the left.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Hold on. Look up, everybody. Over there. Just going now.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was Little Wenna, a yellow star in the Brass Reach. Eleven billion years old. She warmed four planets, and a comet that kept coming back to visit.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: She went out just now, very quietly, the way she did everything.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was Old Corvane, a red dwarf, out past the Long Spiral. Not much to look at. Never was.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: But he burned for a trillion years, steady as anything, and he never once let anybody down.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was Hespera Nine. Blue, very bright, gone young. She used to be the first star out in the evening, on a little moon called Fallow, and every night a child would wish on her.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The child grew up. The wish came true. Hespera never knew. So I'm telling her now.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was the Twins, two stars going round each other, out in the Quiet Arm. They went out at exactly the same moment.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Neither of them had to be the one left. That's lucky, love. That's the luckiest thing I know.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was a little orange star nobody ever named. So I'm naming him now. Gloam. Small, a bit shy, out on the edge of things.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Like us, really. Goodnight, Gloam. You had a name all along.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: That was a star called Patience, the last one in her whole galaxy. She waited a very long time for company.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Then she heard the music. And she held on, just long enough, for one more drop.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Goodnight, love. Thanks for the light. This one's for you.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The guys have their hands up. Lorraine's dimmed a little, out of respect. Here's the next one.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: We'll keep the beat going for you. That's what we do here. Goodnight.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to the Warm-Up. The universe is about two degrees above absolute zero. Let's see what we can do.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The Warm-Up is going well, everybody. We've brought the dance floor up by nearly a whole degree.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The rest of the universe is still freezing. But the dance floor, love. The dance floor is lovely.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Early in the night the beat's still quick, and the guys are fresh. Dov's doing the thing with his arms. It hasn't got a name.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Nothing new has had a name for a very long time. So we'll call it the Dov. Well done, Dov.

lines.speaker: Dov
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: It's late. This is the Long Fade. The beat has come down a long way tonight. Hold on to each other. It's going to be beautiful.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: We've been losing beats all night, and now we're right down where it's slow and deep, and every kick takes its time.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Wendell says it's like dancing under water. Wendell's never seen water. There isn't any left. He's guessing. He's right, though.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Three guys and a nebula, in the dark, at the end of everything, swaying.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: I've played bigger rooms, love. I've never played a better one.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Somewhere in the Long Fade, the guys always stop dancing for a bit, and just stand there, arms round each other, looking up.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Then the beat comes round again, and they start again. That's all any of us are doing, really.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Good morning. This is Morning, Anyway. There's no sun now, so the third guy holds the lamp up as high as he can, and we all say, oh, look. Dawn.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Breakfast at the end of the universe is a flask of tea that Wendell has been keeping warm since the stars were young.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: One cup each. Lorraine has the steam. She says it's the best thing she's had in ages.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: If you're out there, and it's a real morning where you are, with a real sun in it, go and stand in it for a minute, love.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Just for us. We'll keep the music going till you're back.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: This is the last advertisement in the universe.

lines.speaker: Announcer
lines.text: We would like to thank our sponsors. All of them have now closed. They were lovely. They sold lamps, and soup, and blankets, and they always gave you a little bit extra.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Offer ends at the end.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: A message from the afterparty. To conserve heat, please dance close together, wave your arms at least once a song, and keep the door shut.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: There isn't a door. Keep it shut anyway. It's the thought that counts.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Did anyone hear the Quiet Corner last night? Greg's show, on the Lounge at the End of Time. I put my ear right up against the speaker.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: A little breathing, a long pause, and once, very softly, the word, okay. That's an honest show, love. We played it to Lorraine. She liked the pauses.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Someone says a moon's gone missing. Out here, love, we've been missing moons for ages. Most of them, honestly. But a new one? That's nearly news.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The guys are looking under the speakers. Lorraine's checking her pockets. She hasn't got pockets.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Toast. Everything smells of toast. There hasn't been any toast for a hundred trillion years. Dov's crying.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The third guy says, that's my nan's kitchen. That's the most he's ever said. Somebody, somewhere, is making breakfast. Good.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Everybody's humming the same song. Even Lorraine, low and slow, from forty light years off. Nobody knows how it ends.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Maybe it doesn't, love. Let's just keep humming.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Three knocks. Out here. There's no door. There's nothing to knock on for a very long way. The guys have gone very quiet.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Come in, whoever you are. It's warm by the decks.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: The dark has gone a colour. Out here, where nothing has had a colour for ages. Not red. Not blue. Something new. Lorraine's trying to match it.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: First new colour in a trillion years, love. Let's dance in it.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: A pigeon just walked onto the dance floor. At the end of the universe. The guys have never seen a bird. It's walking round each of them, like it knows them.

lines.speaker: DJ Entropy
lines.text: Now it's looking at me. Hello, love. Did you come far?
